title.label: Temper your expectations if you're not rich

content.label:
The app looks and sounds gorgeous. You get 6 soundscapes + their visuals for free. There's also a focus timer, alarm, and breathing exercises available (although the UI is confusing with the Focus / Sleep / Escape "modes"). 

But for the full experience, it feels like you have to be wealthy. The app itself is $5.83/mo or $300 for a lifetime license. There's no Android version, so if I ever wanted to change phones in the future I'd be out $300. 

That price doesn't sound worth it to me for 100 soundscapes alone, so to really make it worth it, I'd want to take advantage of the premium features. I'd need a nice screen for the visuals (like a 4K or better TV), a good set of earphones for the dynamic Spatial Audio, and smart lighting in my home to sync to the soundscape. 

While I'm disappointed this app isn't for me, it does seem really well made. They respect your privacy, and I especially love how you can preview their premium soundscapes before buying.

Portal was great even BEFORE they added Homekit immersive lighting… Try it! Route the audio to your HomePods (or better yet, your AirPods), connect your HomeKit lights, pick an environment, set the volume to a comfortable level and go about your work, reading, relaxing, meditating, sleep or whatever. Before you know it, you’ll forget that you’re sitting in your office. If you need some kind of sound mask to let you sleep, they have that covered too - set the time you want to be awakened and your lights will gently fade on over time (you can choose how gradually and use an audio alarm when it’s time to start your day if you need it.) Great UI, high quality sound and visuals, thoughtful design, many environments and regular updates. Come on, give it a try… whaddya have to lose? Here’s hoping they add a version for Apple TV and AVP down the road as well…!
** edit ** Have I also mentioned their support is second to none? Real humans, real responses, no boilerplate nonsense. Can’t say enough good about the app or the devs!

title.label: A Breath of Color in a Black-and-White World

content.label: Portal is an app that should be studied. It carefully and thoughtfully builds a captivating experience in the name of wellbeing. Upon running the app for the first time, being greeted with a stunning 8K-resolution environment was not only visually surprising, but was accompanied and held the hands of an auditory catharsis of 7.1 Dynamic Spatial Audio originating from the scene you’re placed in. In my home I have several smart lights, and you can imagine my surprise to see that by linking them to Portal, the colors instantly matched the setting, creating a depth of immersion. Instead of the push towards stress and pressure from other productivity apps, Portal encourages clarity and balance. From a circadian-based evolution of a day and night cycle, grants an environment that accompanies you throughout your day, or takes you to the rainforests of St. Lucia, or to Scottish castle walls on a breathtaking loch. All with the purpose of relaxation, sleep, or everyday focus. In an age of data harvesting and spying, Portal is transparent about their removal of analytics, data collection, and ad-trackers. And highlights the processes behind their making of a passion-project that doesn’t have to spell out that lthe team is in it for the long term. From the compassion and sincerity that the small independent team of friends and brothers, it suggests that focus grows gently, like nature itself. It reminded me that true productivity comes from steadiness, not rush. It’s rare to find an application, that feels both practical and nourishing, and this is the only app in which I was truly reminded that clarity, balance, and progress, are rooted in nature.
